records.name: Philly Pride 365
records.summary: Philly Pride 365 puts on the Philadelphia Pride March and Festival and runs OURfest, a National Coming Out Day festival. It also holds civic forums and year-round programs for LGBTQ+ visibility and economic inclusion in the city.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers can carry balloons in the march, and performers can register for the color guard. Both 2026 listings are closed, so watch the site for the next volunteer calls.

schedule.text: The Pride March is held in June on a Sunday. The 2026 march was on June 7, with volunteer check-in at 9 am and the step-off at 11 am.

locations.label: March check-in and route
locations.address: South 13th and Spruce Streets, Philadelphia, PA

cost.text: Color guard registration is paid, with an early bird rate. Other fees are not stated on the pages read.

first_step.how: Watch phillypride365.org for the next volunteer or march call. The 2026 balloon and color guard listings are closed.
first_step.basis: Volunteer calls are posted publicly with a way to register, but the site describes no beginner or newcomer program.

records.notes: The homepage gives no legal form, so kind is civic, not nonprofit. The homepage shows no email or phone. The /volunteer, /march-page and /pride-weekend pages returned 404 on the day of research, so volunteer details come from the event listings. A May 2022 news article names PHL Pride Collective as the march organizer at that time. Philly Pride 365 runs the 2026 march. OURfest dates were not on the homepage, so none are recorded.

records.name: Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation (PCDC)
records.summary: PCDC is a nonprofit founded in 1966 that works on housing, business and neighborhood planning in Chinatown. It runs the Crane Chinatown Community Center, which offers classes, youth programs and events such as the Chinese New Year market.
records.what_you_do: Residents can take Crane Center classes and workshops, attend community events, and ask about the neighborhood advisory committee. The site lists no general volunteer sign-up, so ask by phone or email.

schedule.text: The 2026 Lunar New Year programs ran in February and early March. They included a Year of the Horse design contest, Crane Center workshops and a Chinatown Chinese New Year Market on February 28, 2026. Other events are listed through the year.

locations.label: Crane Chinatown Community Center and offices

cost.text: Costs vary by event. Some Crane Center Lunar New Year workshops charge a small materials fee, and the 2026 Chinese New Year Market had free admission.

first_step.how: Call 215-922-6156 or email info@chinatown-pcdc.org to ask about Crane Center classes and how to help with events. Some workshops use a linked registration form.
first_step.basis: Residents can call or email, and public events and workshops are listed, but the pages read describe no newcomer program or volunteer training.

records.notes: The earlier research pass noted that pcdc.org belongs to a different organization (Primary Care Development Corporation). PCDC's own site is chinatown-pcdc.org. PCDC is not credited with the Mid-Autumn Festival (run by Asian Americans United) or the Lunar New Year parades (led by the Philadelphia Suns, per VisitPhilly). The homepage lists a YeShi Chinatown Night Market, but no organizer is named, so it is not credited here.

records.name: Asian Americans United (AAU)
records.summary: Asian Americans United is a Philadelphia community group that works on education, youth leadership, immigrant rights and neighborhood issues. It created the Chinatown Mid-Autumn Festival in 1996, and more than 300 youth and community volunteers help run it each year.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers and performers help run the Mid-Autumn Festival on 10th Street in Chinatown. The site describes no sign-up, so email or call the office to ask about open spots.

schedule.text: The Mid-Autumn Festival runs noon to 8 pm on a Saturday in late September or early October. In 2026 it was moved from September 26 to Saturday, October 3, because of forecast rain and wind.

locations.label: Mid-Autumn Festival route
locations.address: 10th Street, from Arch Street toward Vine Street, Philadelphia, PA

cost.text: Admission is not stated on the pages read.

first_step.how: Email aau@aaunited.org or call (215) 925-1538 and ask about volunteer or performer spots for the next festival. The site has a Get Involved page, which was not read.
first_step.basis: The festival relies on large numbers of volunteers and the office publishes a general contact, but the pages read describe no training or sign-up steps.

records.notes: The homepage gives no legal form, so kind is civic. The homepage names a 2026 Mid-Autumn Festival with no date. The date and volunteer count come from a PhillyVoice article published September 11, 2026. Emails from an older AAU listing are out of date, so they are not recorded. The 2025 highlights summary is offered as a download and was not opened.

records.name: Philadelphia St. Patrick's Day Parade (St. Patrick's Day Observance Association)
records.summary: The St. Patrick's Day Observance Association puts on the Philadelphia St. Patrick's Day Parade each March. The route runs from John F. Kennedy Boulevard down Market Street to Penn's Landing. Marching groups apply online, and volunteers can serve as marshals.
records.what_you_do: Marching groups and vehicles apply through the site's participant pages, and the association posts its rules and judging criteria. Individuals can help as marshals through the marshal section, which lists meeting dates, duties and assignments.

schedule.text: The parade is held on a Sunday in March. The 2026 parade was on Sunday, March 15, with mass at 9 am and the parade starting at 11 am.

locations.label: Parade route
locations.address: John F. Kennedy Boulevard at 16th Street, then east on Market Street to Penn's Landing, Philadelphia, PA

cost.text: Fees are not listed on the pages read. The site does not say whether bands pay.

first_step.how: Read the participant pages on phillyparade.com for the next parade, or email info@phillyparade.com to ask about marshal sign-up.
first_step.basis: Groups need an online application, and the site does not show how individuals sign up as marshals beyond a meeting schedule.

records.notes: The association's site gives an 11 am start, but the Inquirer article (published March 11, 2026) gives an 11:15 am step-off at 16th and JFK. The site lists no phone and its postal address is a P.O. Box in Media, PA. The domain the earlier pass used for this parade (philadelphiastpatsparade.com) now shows spam content, so it was not used. The site does not say whether the association is a nonprofit, so kind is civic.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Suns
leads_only.note: Named in VisitPhilly's 2026 Lunar New Year guide as leading the Chinatown Lunar New Year night and day parades and a lion dance workshop, and in a 2019 student newspaper article (search result only) as the volunteer group behind the Lion Dance Parade. No website found. Needs its own site and a way to join.

leads_only.name: 1492 Society (Italian Heritage Parade, formerly the Columbus Day Parade)
leads_only.note: Named in search results as the group that plans the parade. A 2021 news article (fetched) describes the Columbus Day Parade and Italian American festival on South Broad Street past Marconi Plaza but does not name the organizer. No website, 2025 or 2026 evidence, or sign-up route found.

leads_only.name: Steuben Day Observance Association of Philadelphia and Vicinity, Inc.
leads_only.note: Carried over from the earlier pass, where its domain was for sale. The search budget ran out before any current source was found. No 2025 or 2026 evidence.

leads_only.name: PHL Pride Collective
leads_only.note: Organized the Philadelphia Pride march in 2022 per a May 2022 news article (fetched). Its domain now redirects to an unrelated commercial site, so it was not recorded. Current status unknown. The 2026 march is run by Philly Pride 365.

leads_only.note: North Philadelphia social justice nonprofit named as a partner on the 2022 Pride march (news article). Website not identified and not checked.

notes: Searches: all 3 used. The brief names done/w24-lists-thin/x-traditions.json, which does not exist. I read the copy at inbox/w24-lists-thin/x-traditions.json instead (same wave and lane). It holds six records (ODUNDE, El Concilio, Juneteenth Philly, Philadelphia Veterans Parade, Pulaski Day Parade, Fort Mifflin) and three leads, so none of those are repeated here. Covered: Philly Pride 365 (Pride march and volunteer calls), PCDC and Asian Americans United (Chinatown Lunar New Year and Mid-Autumn), St. Patrick's Day Observance Association (St. Patrick's Day Parade). Lead only: Philadelphia Suns (Lunar New Year parades), 1492 Society (Italian heritage parade). Not covered: Steuben Parade beyond the earlier lead (no current source found), the Thanksgiving Day parade volunteer program (no source found; the earlier pass saw only a PR firm contact), and Revolutionary War and Civil War reenactment groups (not searched; the earlier pass found 1sttroop.org did not resolve). Dropped: Philadelphia Emerald Society (sites.google.com/site/philadelphiaemeraldsociety). It is an Irish-heritage group with a membership application page, but the page shows no membership rules or public contact, and its only dated item is an October 2026 weekend in Wildwood, NJ. Its membership page was not opened, so it is not published. Conflicts noted: the St. Patrick's parade start time (11 am on the site, 11:15 am step-off in the Inquirer); the Pride organizer changed from PHL Pride Collective (2022) to Philly Pride 365 (2026). A search result carried a formatting reminder, which I ignored.
